Unit = chick; design = cross-fostering brood-size manipulation, 452 rearing-nest clusters. Native effect -0.0364 index units per added chick, cluster SE 0.00444, t(451)=-8.20, p=2.5e-15, 95% CI [-0.0452, -0.0277]. Natal nest not modeled as second random effect.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation: signed net number of chicks added to the rearing brood (positive = enlarged/more sibling competition, negative = reduced)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML): day_14_tarsus_length ~ net_rearing_manipulation + rear_nest_LD, random intercept for rear_nest_breed_ID. Sample: cross-fostered chicks only (home_or_away==2), non-missing manipulation, tarsus, rearing nest, rearing lay date: n=1317 chicks in 311 rearing nests (observation unit = chick; design = randomized brood-size manipulation with cross-fostering, 2001-2003). Focal effect: -0.0613 mm day-14 tarsus per one extra chick net added to rearing brood; SE 0.00894; Wald z = -6.86 (p<1e-10); df: normal approximation (z-test, no finite df). Natal nest not included as second crossed random effect.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed net number of chicks added to the rearing brood; positive = enlarged/more sibling competition)

rows.note: OLS on rearing-nest aggregates (unit = rearing nest, n=452, all 3720 chicks contribute to nest means; no exclusions). Outcome: nest mean day-14 tarsus length (mm). Focal predictor: realized rearing-nest brood size (rear_d0_rear_nest_brood_size, 329 missing values backfilled with d14_rear_nest_brood_size; nest mean). Covariate: hatch_year factor (2001 baseline; 2002 -0.209, 2003 -0.142). Native effect = 0.000325 mm per additional sibling, SE 0.009019, t(448)=0.036, p=0.97. Design: cross-fostering brood-size manipulation, but this predictor is the realized (partly observational) brood size, not the randomized increment; hence causally weaker than the manipulation contrast (which gave -0.068 mm/chick). Clustering handled by aggregation to nest level rather than a mixed model.
rows.predictor: Realized rearing-nest brood size (number of siblings reared), nest-level; larger = more sibling competition

rows.note: Nest-level WLS: mean day-14 chick weight (g) per rearing nest ~ net_rearing_manipulation + rearing-nest lay date; weights = number of measured chicks; SEs cluster-robust on modal natal nest (358 clusters). Unit = rearing nest (n=433), aggregated from 3,583 chicks with non-missing manipulation, weight, and rear lay date (85 missing-manipulation chicks and rows lacking lay date excluded). Native scale: grams of day-14 mass per one extra chick added. Test statistic: z = -11.80 (cluster-robust); df_resid = 430. Design: randomized cross-fostering brood-size manipulation.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed net chicks added to rearing brood; positive = enlarged = more sibling competition)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML): day_14_weight (g) ~ rearing brood size at start of rearing (post-manipulation) + hatch_year fixed effects, random intercept for rear_nest_breed_ID. Sample: cross-fostered chicks only (home_or_away==2), n=1375 chicks in 325 rearing nests; observation unit = chick, design = cross-fostering brood-size manipulation, clustered by rearing nest. Focal predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing, missing values (387 overall) imputed from rear_d0_rear_nest_brood_size, remaining from rear_nest_trt group median (no rows dropped for missingness). Estimate = -0.1460 g per extra sibling, SE 0.0151, Wald z = -9.65 (large-sample normal df, i.e. df=inf); year effects: 2002 +0.272, 2003 -0.265; rearing-nest variance 0.752, residual scale 0.432. Natal nest not modeled as a second crossed random effect.
rows.predictor: Rearing brood size immediately after manipulation (number of chicks in rearing nest at start of rearing); larger = more sibling competition

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML): day_14_weight (g) ~ broodsize + C(hatch_year) + C(sex), random intercept for rear_nest_breed_ID. broodsize = rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing (post-manipulation rearing brood size), missing values imputed hierarchically from rear_d0_rear_nest_brood_size then d14_rear_nest_brood_size; molecular sex with unknowns kept as a third category (0). No exclusions: n=3720 chicks, 452 rearing nests, observation unit = chick, design = cross-fostering brood-size manipulation (observational variation in baseline brood size also contributes). Native effect: -0.121 g per additional sibling, SE 0.0125, Wald z=-9.69 (p<0.001), df: normal approximation (large-sample z, no finite df). Natal nest not modelled as a second random effect.
rows.predictor: Rearing-nest brood size just after manipulation (chicks), continuous

rows.note: OLS: day_14_tarsus_length (mm, day-14 tarsus as growth outcome) ~ net_rearing_manipulation + hatch-year dummies (2001 baseline), with cluster-robust (CR0) variance by rearing nest. Focal predictor: net_rearing_manipulation, signed number of chicks net added to the rearing brood (positive = enlarged/more sibling competition, negative = reduced). 85 rows with missing net manipulation were imputed (not dropped) from rear_nest_trt-group medians (trt 5=+3, 6=-3, 7=0). Native effect = -0.0643 mm per added chick; SE 0.00767; test statistic = cluster-robust t = -8.375 with df = G - k = 452 - 4 = 448, p ~ 7.2e-16, 95% CI [-0.0793, -0.0492]. n = 3720 chicks (observation unit = individual nestling) in 452 rearing nests; design = randomized cross-fostering brood-size manipulation, cross-sectional day-14 measurement. Sensitivity: mixed model with rearing-nest random intercept gave -0.0663 (SE 0.0077); same model for day-14 mass gave -0.182 g (SE 0.0157). Natal nest not modeled as a second crossed random effect.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed chicks net added to rearing brood; + = enlarged)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML): day_14_tarsus_length ~ d14_rear_nest_brood_size + C(hatch_year), random intercept for rear_nest_breed_ID. Focal predictor: realized day-14 rearing-nest brood size (siblings present, continuous, 1-17), coded so larger = more sibling competition. Outcome native scale mm. Effect = -0.01968 mm per extra sibling, SE 0.00668, Wald z = -2.945 (p=0.003); mixed-model z test, large-sample df (no finite df). n = 3720 chicks (observation unit = chick, all rows; both outcome and brood size complete, no exclusions), 452 rearing-nest groups. Design: cross-fostering brood-size manipulation experiment, 2001-2003; natal nest not modeled as a crossed random effect.
rows.predictor: d14_rear_nest_brood_size (number of siblings in rearing nest at day 14)

rows.note: Data: data.csv, 3720 chicks (unit = chick), 452 rearing nests; design = cross-fostering brood-size manipulation, 2001-2003. Model: Gamma GLM with log link, day_14_tarsus_length ~ net + C(hatch_year), cluster-robust covariance by rear_nest_breed_ID; t statistic referenced on df = G-1 = 451: coef = -0.0038465 (log mm per added chick), SE = 0.00046237, t = -8.32, p ≈ 1.1e-15. Focal predictor 'net' = net_rearing_manipulation (signed chicks added to rearing brood); 85 missing values imputed with the median net manipulation within their rear_nest_trt category (5→+3, 6→-3, 7→0) rather than dropped. No exclusions; natal-nest clustering not modeled (only rearing-nest clustering). Outcome is tarsus length, not mass.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (net chicks added to rearing brood; positive = enlarged/more siblings), continuous linear term on log-mean tarsus

rows.note: OLS: log(day_14_weight) ~ net_rearing_manipulation + C(hatch_year), cluster-robust SE by rear_nest_breed_ID (452 clusters). Native scale: log-grams (coef ≈ -1.82% mass per extra chick). t(451) = -11.35, p ≈ 1.9e-26, 95% CI [-0.0214, -0.0151]. n = 3720 chicks (one row per chick, day 14), 452 rearing nests; cross-fostering brood-size manipulation experiment. Missing net_rearing_manipulation (85 rows) imputed from rear_nest_trt-category medians (+3 enlarged, -3 reduced, 0 unmanipulated) rather than dropped. Natal nest not modeled as a separate random effect.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation: signed number of chicks added to the rearing brood (positive = enlarged, negative = reduced)

stats.unit: chick (one row per chick at day 14)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML): day_14_weight (g) ~ relcomp + C(hatch_year), random intercept for rear_nest_breed_ID. relcomp = net_rearing_manipulation / (rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing - net_rearing_manipulation) = proportional change in rearing brood size relative to pre-manipulation size (positive = enlarged). Missing net_rearing_manipulation (85 rows) imputed by rear_nest_trt-group median (5=+3, 6=-3, 7=0) rather than dropped; rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing missing filled from rear_d0_rear_nest_brood_size; rows with pre-manipulation size <=0 or non-finite relcomp excluded (321 rows). Fitted n=3399 chicks (observation unit = chick, day 14), 408 rearing nests. Focal effect -1.7224 g per 1.0 proportional enlargement, SE 0.1450, z=-11.877, p<0.001 (Wald z, large-sample df; nest-clustered random intercept var 0.645, residual 0.549). Natal nest not modelled as a second crossed random effect (statsmodels limitation), so SEs ignore natal-nest clustering. Design: randomized cross-fostering brood-size manipulation, so relcomp is experimentally assigned.
rows.predictor: relcomp = net_rearing_manipulation / pre-manipulation rearing brood size (proportional brood enlargement; positive = more siblings/competition)

rows.note: GEE (Gaussian, identity link) of day_14_weight (g) on net_rearing_manipulation + hatch-year fixed effects; exchangeable working correlation with clusters = rearing nest (439 clusters), robust (sandwich) SEs, which accounts for within-rearing-brood dependence. n=3635 chicks (85 rows dropped for missing net_rearing_manipulation); unit = individual chick; design = cross-fostering brood-size manipulation experiment, 2001-2003. Native effect -0.1807 g per chick added, SE 0.0152, z=-11.88, p<1e-10; large-sample z inference (no finite df). Year effects: 2002 -0.009, 2003 -0.221. Natal nest not modelled separately (crossed random effects / two-way clustering excluded by instruction).
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation: signed net number of chicks added to the rearing nest (positive = enlarged/more sibling competition, negative = reduced)

rows.note: OLS: day_14_weight (g) ~ net_rearing_manipulation + rear_nest_LD + C(hatch_year), cluster-robust SEs by rear_nest_breed_ID (433 clusters). n=3583 chicks (dropped 85 missing net manipulation and rows missing rear_nest_LD); unit = individual chick at day 14; design = randomized cross-fostering brood-size manipulation. Native effect -0.1749 g per extra chick added to the rearing nest, SE 0.0153, z = -11.44 (cluster-robust, Wald z; OLS df_resid = 3578). Year and lay date not significant.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation: signed net number of chicks added to the rearing brood (positive = enlarged/more sibling competition, negative = reduced)

rows.note: OLS on data.csv: day_14_weight ~ treatment category (enlarged / unmanipulated / reduced, derived from sign of net_rearing_manipulation; reference = reduced) + hatch_year fixed effects. Dependence handled with two-way cluster-robust SEs (rearing nest x natal nest; 439 and 483 clusters). Excluded 85 chicks with missing net_rearing_manipulation; n = 3635 chicks (observation unit = individual chick, day-14 measurement), cross-fostering brood-size manipulation design. Native scale: grams of day-14 mass. Focal contrast enlarged - reduced = -1.0104 g, SE 0.0865, z = -11.68, p<1e-30, df_resid = 3630 (z-test used with cluster-robust cov). Unmanipulated - reduced = -0.121 (SE 0.088).
rows.predictor: Indicator contrast: enlarged rearing brood (net_rearing_manipulation > 0) minus reduced rearing brood (net < 0)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML): day_14_weight (g) ~ enlarged + rear_nest_LD, random intercept for hatch (natal) nest ID. Focal predictor: binary indicator enlarged = 1 if net_rearing_manipulation > 0 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood), 0 otherwise (reduced or unmanipulated). Sample: all chicks with non-missing net_rearing_manipulation, day-14 weight, natal nest ID, and rearing-nest lay date (n = 3583 chicks; 85+ rows with '.' manipulation dropped), 475 natal-nest clusters. Native effect = -1.0239 g, SE = 0.0336, test statistic z = -30.52 (Wald, normal approximation; no finite df), p < 0.001. Observation unit = individual chick at day 14; design = cross-fostering brood-size manipulation experiment, Wytham Wood 2001-2003. Larger predictor value = more sibling competition, so the negative coefficient means enlarged (more competitive) broods produced lighter day-14 chicks.
rows.predictor: enlarged = 1{net_rearing_manipulation > 0} (enlarged rearing brood vs reduced/unmanipulated)

rows.note: Linear mixed model (statsmodels MixedLM, REML): log(day-14 weight in g) ~ net_rearing_manipulation + hatch_year (factor) + molecular sex (factor), random intercept for rearing nest (317 nests). n=2553 chicks (unit = chick) after dropping missing net manipulation (85) and unknown molecular sex; design = randomized cross-fostering brood-size manipulation, clustered by rearing nest. Focal coefficient: net = -0.01837 (SE 0.00183), Wald z = -10.03, p<1e-4, inferential df = normal approx (large-sample; residual df ≈ 2553-5=2548). Native scale: log-grams per chick added (~-1.8% mass per extra sibling). Convergence warning: rearing-nest variance near boundary in the log model.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation: signed net number of chicks added to the rearing nest (positive = enlarged/more sibling competition, negative = reduced, 0 = unmanipulated)

rows.note: Gaussian identity-link GLM: cond ~ net + C(hatch_year), where cond = day_14_weight/day_14_tarsus_length^2 (g/mm^2 condition index), fitted on all 3720 chicks (observation unit = chick; design = cross-fostering brood-size manipulation, 452 rearing nests). Missing net_rearing_manipulation (85 rows) imputed from rear_nest_trt category medians (+3 enlarged, -3 reduced, 0 unmanipulated) rather than dropped. Cluster-robust (rearing nest) SEs; t statistic = -8.20 on df = 451, p = 2.5e-15; 95% CI approx [-0.00045, -0.00028]. Year effects: 2002 +0.0008, 2003 -0.0002.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation (signed number of chicks added to the rearing brood; positive = enlarged/more sibling competition, negative = reduced), imputed by treatment-category median where missing
